coverage: Monday 31 Aug 2026 pre-market run (~07:02-07:55 SGT), the first weekday run after the weekend. US/HK/SG cash markets remain closed since Friday 28 Aug's close and have not yet reopened (HKEX/SGX open ~09:00-09:30 SGT later this morning; US opens 21:30 SGT tonight). The price feed's own bars confirm the same known artifact seen over the weekend: pure US-exchange instruments (indices, gold/silver ETFs, miners, USO/XLE) still show no Friday 28 Aug bar, while futures (silver/gold/WTI/Brent) and crypto rolled forward to a genuine Sunday 30 Aug reopen bar, and HK/SG-listed single stocks reached Friday 28 Aug. The dominant genuinely-new development since Sunday's run is a real military escalation: CENTCOM (on record) struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, the first US action against Iran in over a month, corroborated by CNN/CNBC/Al Jazeera; oil futures extended gains into Monday's Asia session as a result. A separate single-sourced claim that Iran retaliated against US forces in Jordan the same day could NOT be corroborated (no CENTCOM/Pentagon/wire-service confirmation) and is explicitly labeled unconfirmed everywhere it's mentioned. Congress: one new filer added (Rep. Jared Moskowitz, immaterial AMAT/STE/GWW managed-account trades). No new insider filings, no new 13F/13D/13G whale activity. A claimed Hong Kong Southbound 'record outflow' figure was checked, found to be a misdated 2025 article, and was NOT published -- flagged in flows-investors.json instead.
tldr: Confirmed escalation, not just rhetoric: CENTCOM struck Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday -- the first US military action on Iran in a month -- pushing oil futures ~2% higher into Monday's Asia open; a separate claim of Iranian retaliation against US forces in Jordan is unconfirmed and should not be treated as fact.

The September Fed-hike debate remains a genuine coin-flip (CME ~56%, Kalshi ~47/54) rather than settling either way -- Goldman/SocGen hawkish vs Brookings economists/Krugman skeptical -- the dominant risk for the levered silver/miners sleeve into the 16 Sep FOMC.

Silver miners' August rally (Hecla +47%, First Majestic +42%, Pan American +22% MTD) still outpaces the metal itself even after Friday's Warsh-driven rout -- the Silver Institute projects a sixth straight annual supply deficit, widening to 46.3M oz. Treat Friday as noise within an intact bullish month.

JPMorgan cut DBS's target to S$63 (from S$70) and downgraded OCBC to underweight on asset-quality/geopolitical-risk concerns -- a direct negative read on two core SGX holdings worth weighing against the sector's still-strong 1H26 income prints.

No new smart-money moves: super-investor, 13F, congress (beyond one immaterial filer) and SGX/HKEX insider checks all came back empty this run -- Friday's GOOGL/Berkshire story remains the dominant recent whale theme, unchanged.

Breadth is broadly participative but losing short-term momentum: 9 of 11 sector ETFs sit above their 200-DMA and %S&P>50-DMA is 52.88%, yet %S&P>200-DMA has declined all week (72.1%->68.8%) and the McClellan Oscillator reads -99.23 (bearish).
